items.title: bug: nested workflow_call overwrites the inner reusable workflow's workflow-level env
items.body:
### Summary

When a reusable workflow is called through two levels of `workflow_call` (A calls B, B calls C), the jobs that come from C lose C's own workflow-level `env:`. They get B's workflow-level env instead. Variables C defines at workflow level are unset in its jobs.

This looks like the nested case left over after #1489 / #1499, which fixed the single-level loss.

### Versions

- Observed on Forgejo 15.0.11, which vendors the runner's `act/jobparser` at v12.10.2.
- In the source, the same logic is in `act/jobparser/jobparser.go` on v12.13.2 and on main.

### Minimal example

`.forgejo/workflows/a.yml`

    on: workflow_dispatch
    env:
      A_LEVEL: a
    jobs:
      call-b:
        uses: ./.forgejo/workflows/b.yml

`.forgejo/workflows/b.yml`

    on: workflow_call
    env:
      B_LEVEL: b
    jobs:
      call-c:
        uses: ./.forgejo/workflows/c.yml

`.forgejo/workflows/c.yml`

    on: workflow_call
    env:
      C_LEVEL: c
    jobs:
      show:
        runs-on: docker
        steps:
          - run: echo "C_LEVEL=${C_LEVEL:-unset} B_LEVEL=${B_LEVEL:-unset}"

Dispatch `a.yml`.

- **Expected:** `C_LEVEL=c B_LEVEL=unset`. A called workflow's workflow-level env applies to its own jobs and does not inherit the caller's.
- **Actual:** `C_LEVEL` is unset, and the job carries B's workflow-level env.

### Cause (from reading the source)

In `expandReusableWorkflow` (`act/jobparser/jobparser.go`), the env of the workflow being expanded is captured with `workflowLevelEnv := workflow.Env`. The function then calls `Parse(contents, ...)` on it, which already expands any deeper `uses:` jobs. Every job that `Parse` returns is re-wrapped with `workflowLevelEnv: workflowLevelEnv`, and the env those jobs already carried (`swf.Env`) is not read. So when A expands B, the jobs that came from C are reassigned B's env, and C's env is lost. Nothing merges the two.

If the inner call's `with:` refers to `needs.*`, expansion is deferred until only one level is left, and the bug does not show. That can hide it in some setups.

### Workaround

Move the env from workflow level to job level in the inner reusable workflows.

### Possible fix

When re-wrapping the jobs that the inner `Parse` returns, keep the workflow-level env a job already carries from a deeper expansion. Assign the expanded workflow's env only to that workflow's own jobs.

items.title: bug: cache server returns lowercased cacheKey on a hit, case-sensitive actions like setup-go re-save their cache every job
items.body:
### Can you reproduce the bug on the Forgejo test instance?

No

### Description

The built-in cache server (`act/artifactcache`) lowercases cache keys when a cache is reserved and when it is looked up, and returns the **lowercased** key as `cacheKey` on a hit. `actions/setup-go` compares that key with its primary key case-sensitively. Its keys contain `Linux`, so it never recognises the exact hit: the restore works, but the post step uploads the whole cache again in every job.

### Affected versions

- Observed on runner v12.13.2, reproduced locally with v13.2.0 (`forgejo-runner exec`).
- Still present in v13.2.1 and on `main` (`80c990d7`); `act/artifactcache` is unchanged since v13.2.0. The lowercasing is in every tag I checked back to v11.0.0 (inherited from nektos/act).

### Root cause

Links point to v13.2.1 (`c4a92ffa`); the files are identical on `main`.

- `find` lowercases the requested keys: [`act/artifactcache/handler.go` L173–L176](https://code.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner/src/commit/c4a92ffa5e3a400ae7e9c40a2914e649eb338ad7/act/artifactcache/handler.go#L173-L176)
- `reserve` lowercases the key before storing it: [`handler.go` L221–L222](https://code.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner/src/commit/c4a92ffa5e3a400ae7e9c40a2914e649eb338ad7/act/artifactcache/handler.go#L221-L222)
- the hit returns the stored, lowercased key: [`handler.go` L200–L204](https://code.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner/src/commit/c4a92ffa5e3a400ae7e9c40a2914e649eb338ad7/act/artifactcache/handler.go#L200-L204) (`"cacheKey": cache.Key`)
- `findCache` matches exactly with `Eq(prefix)`, otherwise by prefix regexp: [`act/artifactcache/caches.go` L121–L148](https://code.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner/src/commit/c4a92ffa5e3a400ae7e9c40a2914e649eb338ad7/act/artifactcache/caches.go#L121-L148)
- the test `case insensitive` asserts the lowercased return value: [`handler_test.go` L569](https://code.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner/src/commit/c4a92ffa5e3a400ae7e9c40a2914e649eb338ad7/act/artifactcache/handler_test.go#L569)

On the client side:

- `@actions/cache` returns the server's `cacheKey` unchanged ([cache.ts](https://github.com/actions/toolkit/blob/0c3a9c332b678ff1e776f93d728a4ad279803abe/packages/cache/src/cache.ts#L284))
- `actions/setup-go` builds its key from `RUNNER_OS` (`setup-go-Linux-…`, [cache-restore.ts L17–L49](https://github.com/actions/setup-go/blob/v7.0.0/src/cache-restore.ts#L17-L49)) and skips the save only if `primaryKey === state` ([cache-save.ts L75–L80](https://github.com/actions/setup-go/blob/v7.0.0/src/cache-save.ts#L75-L80)). `setup-go-Linux-…` !== `setup-go-linux-…`, so it saves again.

`actions/cache` itself is not affected, because its `isExactKeyMatch` ignores case ([actionUtils.ts L19–L26](https://github.com/actions/cache/blob/v6.1.0/src/utils/actionUtils.ts#L19-L26)). Actions that call `@actions/cache` directly and compare strictly (like `setup-go`) are affected.

### Reproduction

Minimal reproduction repository: https://code.forgejo.org/KingOfKalk/forgejo-runner-cache-key-case (hello world + the workflow below, see "Workflow file"). Run it on a runner with the built-in cache server enabled (the default). `check` runs after `fill`, so it restores the entry `fill` saved. Read the `actions/setup-go` and `Post Run actions/setup-go` steps of `check` (logs below).

### Impact

- Every job that uses `setup-go` with caching (the default) uploads its full cache again after a successful restore: about 259 MB per job in this example.
- The cache directory keeps growing with duplicate entries until GC removes unused ones. On one runner it reached ~0.9 GB after a few runs of one small repository.
- Jobs take longer: archive and upload in every post step.

### GitHub behaviour

GitHub's documentation does not say anything about key case. From the official actions:

- `@actions/cache` passes the key returned by the service through unchanged.
- `actions/setup-go` compares it strictly, and does not re-save on GitHub-hosted runners. So GitHub evidently returns the key in the case it was saved with.
- `actions/cache` treats keys that differ only in case as an exact match (since its initial version), which suggests that lookups are case-insensitive.

### Proposed fix

- store and return keys as sent; no lowercasing in `reserve`/`find`
- keep matching case-insensitive in `findCache` (`(?i)` for exact and prefix match)
- backwards compatible: lowercased entries from older runners still match. The first save after the upgrade writes the correctly cased entry, which wins as the newest from then on. No migration needed.

A patch with tests, based on v13.2.1, is on my fork: https://code.forgejo.org/KingOfKalk/runner/compare/v13.2.1...fix/cache-key-case. I can open a PR if this approach is welcome.

### Disclosure

I used AI assistance to locate the relevant code in `act/artifactcache` and to write the tests for the fix. The analysis and the before/after runs were verified on my own runner.

### Forgejo Version

17.0.1

### Runner Version

v12.13.2 (observed), v13.2.0 (reproduced with forgejo-runner exec); code unchanged in v13.2.1 and main (80c990d7)

### How are you running Forgejo?

Official rootless container image (`code.forgejo.org/forgejo/forgejo:17.0.1-rootless`), deployed with the Forgejo Helm chart on k3s (arm64).

### How are you running the Runner?

Official container image (`code.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner:12.13.2`) on k3s (arm64), as a Deployment with a `docker:dind` sidecar. Jobs run in Docker containers (Node 24 / Debian trixie based image). The built-in cache server is enabled with default settings.

### Logs

From the same workflow with Go 1.27.3 (the repository pins 1.27.4, so only the version part of the key differs).

<details>
<summary>Observed (v12.13.2)</summary>

`fill`:
```
Cache is not found
Cache Size: ~259 MB (271682666 B)
Cache saved with the key: setup-go-Linux-arm64-node24trixie-go-1.27.3-8945b2c3…
```

`check`:
```
Cache restored from key: setup-go-linux-arm64-node24trixie-go-1.27.3-8945b2c3…
Cache Size: ~259 MB (271617158 B)
Cache saved with the key: setup-go-Linux-arm64-node24trixie-go-1.27.3-8945b2c3…
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Expected (what a runner with the proposed fix logs)</summary>

`check`:
```
Cache restored from key: setup-go-Linux-arm64-node24trixie-go-1.27.3-8945b2c3…
Cache hit occurred on the primary key setup-go-Linux-arm64-node24trixie-go-1.27.3-8945b2c3…, not saving cache.
```
</details>

### Workflow file

From [`.forgejo/workflows/cache-key-case.yml`](https://code.forgejo.org/KingOfKalk/forgejo-runner-cache-key-case/src/branch/main/.forgejo/workflows/cache-key-case.yml) in the reproduction repository:

```yaml
on: [push, workflow_dispatch]

jobs:
  fill:
    runs-on: docker
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache-dependency-path: go.mod
      - run: go run .

  check:
    needs: fill
    runs-on: docker
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache-dependency-path: go.mod
      - run: go run .
```
